<!-- generated from maestro item 1422 — do not edit; the board item is the source of truth -->
Add an optional django-mojo ACME delegation hub. A downstream deployment authenticates with a protected project API key, allocates an opaque permanent target in one hub-owned public Route53 zone, and publishes/withdraws DNS-01 TXT challenge leases. The hub verifies the tenant's permanent one-hop CNAME before publish. Direct providers and Maestro Sites HTTP-01 are untouched.

---

## Spec

Kind: feature · Requested by: Ian Starnes · Builds before #1423 and #1421

### API contract

All routes require an ApiKey whose underlying key has protected permission dnsman_acme_federation and whose project group is active. JWT users, group tokens, anonymous callers, permissionless keys and privilege-override sessions without underlying permission are denied.

- POST /api/dnsman/acme/delegation
  Body: domain plus immutable downstream client_ref.
  Idempotent for project UUID plus client_ref. Same ref/different domain is refused; a new ref always gets a new target, including the same domain after re-onboarding.
- POST /api/dnsman/acme/challenge/publish
  Body: client_ref, immutable challenge_ref, and the complete digest set.
  Verifies the stored source is exactly one CNAME hop to the stored target, persists a challenge lease, reconciles the union of all active leases, writes the exact target RRset and waits for authoritative visibility.
- POST /api/dnsman/acme/challenge/withdraw
  Body: client_ref and challenge_ref.
  Idempotently retires only that lease and reconciles remaining values. It deliberately does not require the tenant CNAME still to exist, so cleanup cannot be blocked by revocation.

Responses echo only bounded identifiers/counts and the allocation source/target. They never expose hosted-zone ids, AWS change ids, credentials, unrelated targets or TXT digests.

### Persistence and concurrency

- AcmeHubDelegation is an immutable tombstone keyed by owner project UUID plus client_ref. It stores normalized domain/source, random target, original group attribution, allocation zone name/id, and timestamps. It has no deletion or generic CRUD API.
- AcmeHubChallengeLease is keyed by allocation plus challenge_ref and stores the exact active values, state, expiry and reconciliation timestamps.
- The lease is committed before a network write. A per-allocation database/advisory lock serializes complete Route53 reconciliation across processes. Publish/withdraw retries use the same challenge_ref.
- A scheduled sweeper expires stale/pending leases and reconciles their targets, covering worker death and ambiguous Route53 responses.
- Configuration rotation affects new allocations only; every existing allocation remains bound to its stored exact public zone.

### Configuration and security

File-only settings:
- DNSMAN_ACME_HUB_ZONE (feature disabled when absent)
- DNSMAN_ACME_HUB_HOSTED_ZONE_ID (optional exact zone id)
- DNSMAN_ACME_HUB_TTL (default 60)
- bounded lease lifetime and reconciliation timing settings

Every allocation/write validates an exact public Route53 zone and public DNS cut. The zone writer is internal and unavailable to tenant record REST. Rate limits apply per project and IP with ApiKey overrides. Audit allocation, publish/refusal, withdrawal, expiry and provider failure with project/key/request attribution and counts, never credentials or TXT values.

### Compatibility

The hub is dormant by default. It does not add Domain.provider, alter services/certs.py, or change Route53, GoDaddy, or Maestro Sites HTTP-01. Only explicitly configured #1423 clients call it; failures are loud and never trigger fallback.

## Plan

1. Add protected API-key permission and endpoint authentication that rejects inactive/deleted group identity.
2. Add AcmeHubDelegation and AcmeHubChallengeLease models with immutable project UUID/client_ref ownership, permanent allocation tombstones, active lease state and indexes.
3. Add shared authoritative one-hop CNAME verification in mojo/helpers/dns/probe.py.
4. Implement exact public Route53 zone resolution and allocation. Generate opaque 128-bit DNS-safe targets and bind each permanently to its allocation zone.
5. Implement publish/withdraw as challenge-ref idempotent lease transitions plus serialized RRset reconciliation. Persist desired state before AWS calls and add a scheduled stale-lease reconciler.
6. Add custom API endpoints, strict serializers, rate limits, safe error mapping and audit events. No generic model/zone CRUD.
7. Test auth floor, cross-project isolation, target non-reuse, config/zone safety, CNAME refusal, additive apex+wildcard values, parallel leases, ambiguous writes, crashes/sweeper, withdrawal after CNAME removal, safe logging and unchanged direct providers.
8. Update django/web dnsman documentation and settings reference. After migration authorization run bin/create_testproject and use the batch's one closing full suite.

### Challenge

| Objection | Disposition |
|---|---|
| Row-lock plus live RRset union loses cleanup state if the process dies after Route53 writes | Amended: durable challenge_ref leases are committed before writes and swept/reconciled after crashes. |
| Concurrent processes can still race after a short DB transaction | Amended: per-allocation lock covers full desired-state reconciliation; Route53 always receives the union of durable active leases. |
| DELETE request bodies are not reliably carried by every proxy | Amended: explicit POST publish and POST withdraw endpoints. |
| Keying only by project/domain could let an old CNAME prove a later tenant claim | Amended: downstream supplies a fresh immutable client_ref; targets are never reused. |
| Zone configuration rotation could orphan permanent targets | Amended: zone name/id are stored on every allocation and validated on each use. |
| CNAME revocation could block cleanup | Rebutted: publish requires current proof; owner-scoped withdraw never requires the CNAME. |
